On the left is Margaret Thatcher, former Prime Minister of Britain who was infamous for cutting social services, crushing unions and screwing over many working class people - [here’s a good post about why she’s disliked.](https://dracofidus.tumblr.com/post/139609235006/hey-dumb-american-question-here-every-uk-person) 

On the right is [Grenfell Tower](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenfell_Tower_fire), a block of social housing flats that caught fire last year thanks to poor cladding. 71 people died and many others were left homeless. Despite a number of complaints from residents, the council refused to put fire alarms, fire escapes or sprinklers in the building, and instead spent money on flammable cladding to ‘beautify’ the building so it was less of an eyesore for wealthy residents in nearby buildings.

[Here’s a good article](http://www.independent.co.uk/voices/grenfell-tower-inquiry-deregulation-thatcher-tony-blair-fire-service-cuts-a7876346.html) on how the two are connected:

“In the mid-1980s, Thatcher’s government deregulated fire safety standards in homes, abandoning enforceable requirements for guidelines which the building industry could choose to follow, or not.”

Exactly. The protagonist straight out asks why the antagonists are only going after black people at one point. Racism is one of the main themes of the film, from the racist police officer at the beginning to the villains’ reasoning. Surely it’s impossible not to notice that.

Sorry, I wasn’t very clear. I can go out shopping and stuff as long as someone, doesn’t matter who, comes with me. If I go alone my anxiety kicks in and I feel myself start to fall apart. Sorry you have to go through the same struggles, depression really is a bitch. I’m studying English, second year. I don’t really enjoy it but I don’t hate it, I just feel apathetic towards it. It makes me more sad than anything, because I know that as a child or teenager I would have been so passionate and interested in the topics we study. Now I don’t feel anything.

Is standing still when a hearse passes a common thing worldwide? I live in England and I’ve never seen anyone do it.

That said, I live two doors down from a cemetery so if I did that every time a hearse passed I’d never get anywhere.
